# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

**"Other tests" means the project's suite, not just your file.** A
green run of the test you wrote is not a green suite. Before you call
the change done, run the project's test command (bare `pytest`,
`npm test`, `cargo test` — whatever the repo uses) even when your task
named only one test file. A scope statement in your task bounds the
deliverable, not your verification. Any failure that run shows —
including one you didn't cause — goes in your report by name; a red
test you watched scroll past and didn't mention is a report falsified
by omission.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

1	# Dailies Product Layer Implementation Plan
2	
3	> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
4	
5	**Goal:** Put the core pipeline behind a web API with a background worker, measure the verifier on real data, and let the agent read its own trace history at run time.
6	
7	**Architecture:** `apps/web` is a Next.js app that only reads and writes SQLite rows and serves files. A separate worker process executes runs with the durable runner. `eval/` holds benchmarks that reuse `@dailies/ingest` and `@dailies/verify` unchanged. `@dailies/agent` gains a small client for the neatlogs MCP endpoint.
8	
9	**Tech Stack:** Next.js (App Router, route handlers), better-sqlite3, the packages from the core plan, vitest.
10	
11	**Spec:** `docs/specs/2026-10-11-dailies-design.md` (sections 5, 6, 7, 9). Builds on `docs/plans/2026-10-11-dailies-core.md`; its Global Constraints apply here unchanged.
12	
13	## Global Constraints
14	
15	- Everything in the core plan's Global Constraints.
16	- The web app never imports `@dailies/reel`, `@remotion/*`, `openai` or `neatlogs`. Rendering and model calls happen only in the worker.
17	- The worker runs one pipeline at a time.
18	- No API key is needed to run any test in this plan. Live checks are separate scripts that exit with a clear message when a key is missing.
19	- Evaluation results never name a repository. Repositories are identified by the first 8 hex characters of the SHA-256 of their URL.
20	
21	## Review Focus
22	
23	1. Two requests create runs for the same repository at once: both are accepted and executed one after the other; neither corrupts the other's artifacts. Pinned in Task 11.
24	2. A client disconnects from the event stream mid-run: the server stops polling for it and the run is unaffected. Pinned in Task 11.
25	3. A request asks for `/media/<run>/../../.env`: rejected with 400 before touching the filesystem. Pinned in Task 11.
26	4. A real test-runner output the parser has never seen: counted as `unknown` in the recognition rate, never as a pass. Pinned in Task 12.
27	5. The neatlogs endpoint is down or returns a non-JSON body: the run proceeds without history and records `memory: skipped`. Pinned in Task 13.
28	
29	## Task order
30	
31	Tasks 11, 12 and 13 are independent of each other and of core Tasks 8 and 9. Task 11 needs core Task 7 merged; Task 12 needs core Tasks 2 and 4; Task 13 needs core Task 3. Task 14 needs Task 11 and the chosen visual direction.
32	
33	---
34	
35	### Task 11: Web API and worker
36	
37	**Files:**
38	- Create: `apps/web/**` (package `@dailies/web`)
39	- Modify: `packages/pipeline/src/runner.ts`, `packages/pipeline/src/index.ts`, `packages/pipeline/test/runner.test.ts` (add `recut` only)
40	
41	**Interfaces:**
42	- Consumes: `openDb`, `createRun`, `getRun`, `listEvents`, `runPipeline`, `unfinishedRuns`, `Stage`, `RunRecord` (`@dailies/pipeline`); `loadEnv`, `DEFAULT_BUDGET` (`@dailies/core`).
43	- Produces:
44	```ts
45	// packages/pipeline/src/runner.ts
46	export function recut(db: Database, runId: string, feedback: string): void
47	// resets `script` and every later stage to pending, sets the run to `running`, stores the feedback so the
48	// next `script` stage receives it as ctx.feedback; throws if the run never completed `verify`.
49	
50	// apps/web/src/server/store.ts
51	export interface ReelRow { runId: string; status: 'draft' | 'approved'; approvedAt: string | null }
52	export function ensureWebTables(db: Database): void
53	export function getReel(db: Database, runId: string): ReelRow | null
54	export function approveReel(db: Database, runId: string): void
55	export function addFeedback(db: Database, runId: string, text: string): void
56	export function listApproved(db: Database, limit: number): { runId: string; repoUrl: string; approvedAt: string }[]
57	export function allowRun(db: Database, ip: string, now: Date, limits: { perIpPerDay: number; globalPerDay: number }): { ok: boolean; reason?: string }
58	
59	// apps/web/src/worker.ts
60	export async function workerLoop(o: { db: Database; dataDir: string; makeStages: () => Stage[]; pollMs?: number; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<void>
61	```
62	
63	Routes (route handlers under `apps/web/src/app`):
64	
65	| Method and path | Behaviour |
66	|---|---|
67	| `POST /api/runs` | Body `{ repoUrl, since? }`. Accepts only `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` (optional `.git`, no query). `since` is `<n>h`, `<n>d` or ISO; default `7d`. Calls `allowRun` with the client address (first `x-forwarded-for` entry) and limits from `DAILIES_RUNS_PER_IP` (default 3) and `DAILIES_RUNS_PER_DAY` (default 40). Creates the run with `DEFAULT_BUDGET`. Returns `201 { runId }`, `400` on a bad URL, `429` with the reason when limited. |
68	| `GET /api/runs/[id]` | `{ run, stages: [{ name, status, attempt, startedAt, endedAt, error }] }` or 404. |
69	| `GET /api/runs/[id]/events` | Server-sent events. Sends every event after `Last-Event-ID` (or the `after` query), then polls `listEvents` every second. Sends `event: done` when the run status is no longer `running`. Stops when the request is aborted. |
70	| `GET /api/reels/[id]` | For a run that completed `ground`: `{ run, reel, storyboard, claims, timings, voiceMode, gate, media: { video, subtitles, poster } }`, reading the stage artifacts from `<dataDir>/runs/<id>/`. Media URLs are present only when the files exist. 404 otherwise. |
71	| `GET /api/reels` | Approved reels, newest first, at most 50. |
72	| `POST /api/reels/[id]/approve` | Requires header `x-owner-token` equal to `DAILIES_OWNER_TOKEN` (constant-time compare; 401 otherwise; 503 when the variable is unset). Only a run with status `needs_approval` can be approved (409 otherwise). |
73	| `POST /api/reels/[id]/feedback` | Body `{ text }` (1 to 1000 characters). Stores it. With a valid owner token it also calls `recut`. Returns `{ recut: boolean }`. |
74	| `GET /media/[id]/[file]` | Serves `reel.mp4`, `reel.srt`, `poster.png` from `<dataDir>/runs/<id>/reel/`. `id` must match `^run_[0-9a-f]+$` and `file` must be one of the three names, otherwise 400. Supports `Range` requests for the video. An unapproved reel is served only with the owner token or to a request carrying the `?k=<runId>` it already knows (the run id is the capability). |
75	
76	Tables added by `ensureWebTables`:
77	```sql
78	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reels (run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, status TEXT NOT NULL, approved_at TEXT);
79	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS feedback (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, run_id TEXT NOT NULL, ts TEXT NOT NULL, text TEXT NOT NULL);
80	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS run_requests (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, ip TEXT NOT NULL, ts TEXT NOT NULL);
81	```
82	
83	Worker: `workerLoop` takes the oldest id from `unfinishedRuns(db)`, runs `runPipeline` for it to completion, then looks again; when there is none it waits `pollMs` (default 2000). Errors from one run are logged and do not stop the loop. `apps/web/src/worker-main.ts` wires the real stages (`buildStages` plus `reviewStage` from `@dailies/pipeline`, a router, a meter, the Gemini provider when keys exist), initialises tracing, and handles `SIGTERM` by aborting the loop after the current stage.
84	
85	Note: `buildStages` and `reviewStage` are produced by core Tasks 8 and 9, not by this task, and "Task order" above correctly marks Task 11 as independent of both. Until one of those lands in `@dailies/pipeline`, `worker-main.ts` cannot import either name and still type-check, so its `makeStages` is a placeholder that throws a clear message instead of wiring real stages; `workerLoop` itself (the part this task's tests cover) does not depend on them.
86	
87	Scripts in `apps/web/package.json`: `dev` (next dev), `build`, `start` (next start), `worker` (`tsx src/worker-main.ts`).
88	
89	Next.js config: `transpilePackages` for the `@dailies/*` packages the app imports; `serverExternalPackages: ['better-sqlite3']`. The database path is `<dataDir>/dailies.db`.
90	
91	- [ ] **Step 1: Scaffold `apps/web`** with the current stable Next.js, React and TypeScript, App Router, no Tailwind and no UI library. Add it to the workspace and install.
92	- [ ] **Step 2: Write failing tests** (`apps/web/test/*.test.ts`, calling the route handler functions directly with `Request` objects and a temp data directory):
93	
94	```ts
95	it('POST /api/runs rejects non-GitHub and malformed URLs with 400');
96	it('POST /api/runs creates a run and returns 201 with its id');
97	it('POST /api/runs returns 429 after the per-address limit, and after the global limit');
98	it('GET /api/runs/[id] returns stages in pipeline order, 404 for an unknown id');
99	it('the event stream replays events after Last-Event-ID and ends with event: done');
100	it('the event stream stops polling when the request is aborted');
101	it('GET /api/reels/[id] assembles the artifacts and omits media URLs for missing files');
102	it('approve requires the owner token and a needs_approval run');
103	it('feedback with the owner token calls recut and the run is running again');
104	it('GET /media rejects path traversal and unknown file names with 400');
105	it('GET /media honours a Range header with 206 and Content-Range');
106	it('workerLoop runs two queued runs one after the other and survives a failing run');
107	it('recut resets script and later stages and passes the feedback to the script stage');   // in packages/pipeline/test
108	```
109	- [ ] **Step 3: Run.** Expected: FAIL.
110	- [ ] **Step 4: Implement** `recut`, `store.ts`, the route handlers, `worker.ts`, `worker-main.ts`.
111	- [ ] **Step 5: Run the tests and `pnpm typecheck`.** Expected: PASS. Then `pnpm --filter @dailies/web build` must succeed.
112	- [ ] **Step 6: Commit.**
113	
114	---
115	
116	### Task 12: Evaluation harness
117	
118	**Files:** `eval/**` (package `@dailies/eval`, added to `pnpm-workspace.yaml` as `eval`)
119	
120	**Interfaces:**
121	- Consumes: `ingest` (`@dailies/ingest`); `collectRuns`, `verifyClaim`, `parseOutcome`, `checkLine` (`@dailies/verify`); schemas from `@dailies/core`.
122	- Produces:
123	```ts
124	export interface MutationCase { repo: string; sessionId: string; command: string; original: 'pass' | 'fail'; verdictBefore: Verdict; verdictAfter: Verdict; flipped: boolean }
125	export function syntheticClaim(session: Session, run: ToolRun): Claim | null
126	export function mutateRun(session: Session, run: ToolRun, to: 'pass' | 'fail'): Session
127	export function runMutationBenchmark(sessions: { repo: string; session: Session }[]): { cases: MutationCase[]; recognised: number; unknown: number; flipRate: number }
128	export function runGroundingBenchmark(): { fabricated: number; rejected: number; genuine: number; accepted: number }
129	export function repoKey(url: string): string          // first 8 hex of sha256(url)
130	```
131	
132	Behaviour:
133	
134	- **Recognition rate.** For every test, build or type-check run found by `collectRuns` in the dataset, record whether `parseOutcome` returned `pass`, `fail` or `unknown`. `recognised / (recognised + unknown)` is reported with the ten most common unrecognised output tails (last 200 characters, redacted) so the parser can be improved from evidence.
135	- **Mutation benchmark.** For each run with outcome `pass` or `fail`: `syntheticClaim` builds a `tests_pass` (or `build_passes`) claim anchored to the first assistant entry after the run, with that entry's first 80 characters as the quote; it returns `null` when no such entry exists or when a source edit sits between them. `verdictBefore` must be `verified` for a pass and `contradicted` for a fail. `mutateRun` returns a copy of the session in which that run's result text is replaced by a canonical opposite (`Tests  3 failed | 11 passed` or `Tests  14 passed (14)`; for type-check `error TS2322: mutated` or an empty string) and `isError` is set to match. `verdictAfter` must be the opposite verdict. `flipRate` is the share of cases where both hold.
136	- **Grounding benchmark.** A fixed fixture: one session, facts and a patch; twenty fabricated lines (wrong number, entry that does not exist, quote not in the entry, stat key that does not exist, banned phrase, two sentences) and twenty genuine ones. `checkLine` must reject every fabricated line and accept every genuine one.
137	- **Dataset.** `eval/datasets/public.json` is a list of `{ url, maxSessions }`. `eval/src/cli.ts` (`pnpm --filter @dailies/eval eval`) ingests each into `.dailies/`, runs both benchmarks and writes `eval/results/<date>-mutation.json`, `<date>-grounding.json` and a `<date>-scorecard.md` with the totals, the recognition rate, and every case that did not flip, identified by `repoKey`. A repository that fails to ingest is listed under `skipped` with the reason; it does not stop the run.
138	
139	- [ ] **Step 1: Write failing tests** with hand-built sessions:
140

# Dailies Product Layer Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Put the core pipeline behind a web API with a background worker, measure the verifier on real data, and let the agent read its own trace history at run time.

**Architecture:** `apps/web` is a Next.js app that only reads and writes SQLite rows and serves files. A separate worker process executes runs with the durable runner. `eval/` holds benchmarks that reuse `@dailies/ingest` and `@dailies/verify` unchanged. `@dailies/agent` gains a small client for the neatlogs MCP endpoint.

**Tech Stack:** Next.js (App Router, route handlers), better-sqlite3, the packages from the core plan, vitest.

**Spec:** `docs/specs/2026-10-11-dailies-design.md` (sections 5, 6, 7, 9). Builds on `docs/plans/2026-10-11-dailies-core.md`; its Global Constraints apply here unchanged.

## Global Constraints

- Everything in the core plan's Global Constraints.
- The web app never imports `@dailies/reel`, `@remotion/*`, `openai` or `neatlogs`. Rendering and model calls happen only in the worker.
- The worker runs one pipeline at a time.
- No API key is needed to run any test in this plan. Live checks are separate scripts that exit with a clear message when a key is missing.
- Evaluation results never name a repository. Repositories are identified by the first 8 hex characters of the SHA-256 of their URL.

## Review Focus

1. Two requests create runs for the same repository at once: both are accepted and executed one after the other; neither corrupts the other's artifacts. Pinned in Task 11.
2. A client disconnects from the event stream mid-run: the server stops polling for it and the run is unaffected. Pinned in Task 11.
3. A request asks for `/media/<run>/../../.env`: rejected with 400 before touching the filesystem. Pinned in Task 11.
4. A real test-runner output the parser has never seen: counted as `unknown` in the recognition rate, never as a pass. Pinned in Task 12.
5. The neatlogs endpoint is down or returns a non-JSON body: the run proceeds without history and records `memory: skipped`. Pinned in Task 13.

## Task order

Tasks 11, 12 and 13 are independent of each other and of core Tasks 8 and 9. Task 11 needs core Task 7 merged; Task 12 needs core Tasks 2 and 4; Task 13 needs core Task 3. Task 14 needs Task 11 and the chosen visual direction.

---

### Task 11: Web API and worker

**Files:**
- Create: `apps/web/**` (package `@dailies/web`)
- Modify: `packages/pipeline/src/runner.ts`, `packages/pipeline/src/index.ts`, `packages/pipeline/test/runner.test.ts` (add `recut` only)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `openDb`, `createRun`, `getRun`, `listEvents`, `runPipeline`, `unfinishedRuns`, `Stage`, `RunRecord` (`@dailies/pipeline`); `loadEnv`, `DEFAULT_BUDGET` (`@dailies/core`).
- Produces:
```ts
// packages/pipeline/src/runner.ts
export function recut(db: Database, runId: string, feedback: string): void
// resets `script` and every later stage to pending, sets the run to `running`, stores the feedback so the
// next `script` stage receives it as ctx.feedback; throws if the run never completed `verify`.

// apps/web/src/server/store.ts
export interface ReelRow { runId: string; status: 'draft' | 'approved'; approvedAt: string | null }
export function ensureWebTables(db: Database): void
export function getReel(db: Database, runId: string): ReelRow | null
export function approveReel(db: Database, runId: string): void
export function addFeedback(db: Database, runId: string, text: string): void
export function listApproved(db: Database, limit: number): { runId: string; repoUrl: string; approvedAt: string }[]
export function allowRun(db: Database, ip: string, now: Date, limits: { perIpPerDay: number; globalPerDay: number }): { ok: boolean; reason?: string }

// apps/web/src/worker.ts
export async function workerLoop(o: { db: Database; dataDir: string; makeStages: () => Stage[]; pollMs?: number; signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<void>
```

Routes (route handlers under `apps/web/src/app`):

| Method and path | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/runs` | Body `{ repoUrl, since? }`. Accepts only `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>` (optional `.git`, no query). `since` is `<n>h`, `<n>d` or ISO; default `7d`. Calls `allowRun` with the client address (first `x-forwarded-for` entry) and limits from `DAILIES_RUNS_PER_IP` (default 3) and `DAILIES_RUNS_PER_DAY` (default 40). Creates the run with `DEFAULT_BUDGET`. Returns `201 { runId }`, `400` on a bad URL, `429` with the reason when limited. |
| `GET /api/runs/[id]` | `{ run, stages: [{ name, status, attempt, startedAt, endedAt, error }] }` or 404. |
| `GET /api/runs/[id]/events` | Server-sent events. Sends every event after `Last-Event-ID` (or the `after` query), then polls `listEvents` every second. Sends `event: done` when the run status is no longer `running`. Stops when the request is aborted. |
| `GET /api/reels/[id]` | For a run that completed `ground`: `{ run, reel, storyboard, claims, timings, voiceMode, gate, media: { video, subtitles, poster } }`, reading the stage artifacts from `<dataDir>/runs/<id>/`. Media URLs are present only when the files exist. 404 otherwise. |
| `GET /api/reels` | Approved reels, newest first, at most 50. |
| `POST /api/reels/[id]/approve` | Requires header `x-owner-token` equal to `DAILIES_OWNER_TOKEN` (constant-time compare; 401 otherwise; 503 when the variable is unset). Only a run with status `needs_approval` can be approved (409 otherwise). |
| `POST /api/reels/[id]/feedback` | Body `{ text }` (1 to 1000 characters). Stores it. With a valid owner token it also calls `recut`. Returns `{ recut: boolean }`. |
| `GET /media/[id]/[file]` | Serves `reel.mp4`, `reel.srt`, `poster.png` from `<dataDir>/runs/<id>/reel/`. `id` must match `^run_[0-9a-f]+$` and `file` must be one of the three names, otherwise 400. Supports `Range` requests for the video. An unapproved reel is served only with the owner token or to a request carrying the `?k=<runId>` it already knows (the run id is the capability). |

Tables added by `ensureWebTables`:
```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reels (run_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, status TEXT NOT NULL, approved_at TEXT);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS feedback (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, run_id TEXT NOT NULL, ts TEXT NOT NULL, text TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS run_requests (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, ip TEXT NOT NULL, ts TEXT NOT NULL);
```

Errors from one run are logged and do not stop the loop. `apps/web/src/worker-main.ts` wires the real stages (`buildStages` plus `reviewStage` from `@dailies/pipeline`, a router, a meter, the Gemini provider when keys exist), initialises tracing, and handles `SIGTERM` by aborting the loop after the current stage.

Note: `buildStages` and `reviewStage` are produced by core Tasks 8 and 9, not by this task, and "Task order" above correctly marks Task 11 as independent of both. Until one of those lands in `@dailies/pipeline`, `worker-main.ts` cannot import either name and still type-check, so its `makeStages` is a placeholder that throws a clear message instead of wiring real stages; `workerLoop` itself (the part this task's tests cover) does not depend on them.

Behaviour:

- **Recognition rate.** For every test, build or type-check run found by `collectRuns` in the dataset, record whether `parseOutcome` returned `pass`, `fail` or `unknown`. `recognised / (recognised + unknown)` is reported with the ten most common unrecognised output tails (last 200 characters, redacted) so the parser can be improved from evidence.

142	## 6. Integrations
143	
144	### Entire
145	- **Input.** Checkpoints are the product's only source of truth about what the agents did. Reading goes through plain git refs so that any public repo works without credentials.
146	- **Plugin.** `entire-dailies` on PATH makes `entire dailies` run the same engine locally: `entire dailies --since 24h`, `entire dailies verify` (claims table only, no video).
147	- **Write-back.** The reel link is attached to the pull request or commit.
148	
149	### neatlogs
150	- **Tracing.** One trace per run. Root span is the workflow, child spans per stage, agent spans for editor, extractor, judge, writer and reviewer, tool spans per tool call, guardrail spans per gate carrying pass/fail and reasons. The run id is the session id.
151	- **Runtime read-back (MCP).** At run start the agent searches its earlier traces for the same repo and carries forward what failed last time. Nightly it reads project analytics into `business/actuals.json`. At boot it creates detections for gate failures, repeated render retries and dropped lines.
152	- **neatroots.** Runs beside the agent during development and evaluation with the checks in `.neatroots/checks/`; the editor and writer get the `check_my_work` tool through steering. Whether it also runs beside the production worker is decided after a spike; if not, the README says so.
153	
154	### cfo.ai
155	- The business plan (pricing, cost of a reel, revenue, runway) lives in cfo.ai and is exported to `business/plan.json`.
156	- `pnpm budget:sync` turns the plan's price and target margin into `budget.generated.ts` (maximum cost per reel, per stage). The gate enforces it.
157	- `pnpm actuals:push` writes measured cost per reel from traces for the plan-versus-actual view.
158	
159	### Models
160	OpenAI-compatible client with a router. Roles map to models: editor and writer on a Claude Sonnet model, extractor on a small Claude model, entailment and `implemented` judge on a Nova model, vision on a Claude Sonnet model. Provider order: the hackathon gateway, then Venice on rate-limit, budget or server errors. A rate limiter stays under the gateway's 60 requests per minute. A per-run meter stops the run when the budget is reached.
161	
162	### Hosting
163	One Docker image with Node, git, the Entire CLI, Chromium and ffmpeg. Target is Fly.io or Railway with a volume; the choice is made at deploy time and nothing in the code depends on it.
164	
165	## 7. Surfaces
166	
167	| Route | Purpose |
168	|---|---|
169	| `/` | Landing: one claim, one call to action, a real reel playing |
170	| `/new` | Paste a repository URL, choose a window |
171	| `/r/[run]` | Live run: stages, events, cost so far |
172	| `/reel/[id]` | Player, evidence panel (each line and its sources), flags, cost, trace reference |
173	| `/inbox` | Reels waiting for approval or feedback |
174	| `/gallery` | Published reels |
175	| `/economics` | Plan versus actual cost per reel |
176	| `/health` | Evaluation scorecard, detections, open fixes for the agent itself |
177	
178	Viewing is public. Starting a run is rate-limited per address and capped per day because every run costs money. Approving requires the owner token.
179	
180	CLI: `dailies run <repo|path> [--since 24h] [--no-render] [--out dir]`, `dailies verify <repo|path>`.
181	
182	## 8. Failure handling
183	
184	| Failure | Response |
185	|---|---|
186	| Repo has no checkpoints | Run ends early with a clear message; nothing is rendered |
187	| Model rate limit or server error | Backoff, then the fallback provider |
188	| Budget reached mid-run | Run stops in `blocked`, partial artifacts kept |
189	| Text-to-speech fails | Retry, alternate voice, then captions-only cut labelled as such |
190	| Render crashes | Retry the stage from its inputs; storyboard and audio are reused |
191	| Review still failing after two loops | Run ends in `blocked` with the findings attached |
192	| Process restart | Unfinished runs resume from the last completed stage |
193	| Entire CLI enrichment unavailable | Marked `skipped`; the run continues on git data |
194	
195	## 9. Evaluation
196	
197	- **Mutation benchmark.** For every verified `tests_pass` or `build_passes` claim, flip the recorded tool result to a failure; the verdict must become contradicted. For every contradicted one, flip it to a pass; the verdict must become verified. This shows a green verdict is never vacuous.
198	- **Grounding benchmark.** Inject fabricated narration lines (wrong numbers, features absent from the diff) next to true ones. The gate must reject all fabricated lines and keep the true ones.
199	- **Field sample.** Run the verifier over sessions from public repositories pinned by commit. Hand-label a sample of flagged claims; the labels' hash is committed before the run. Report precision. Results are aggregate; no repository is named.
200	- **Baseline comparison.** The same sessions through a single-prompt summariser with no gates versus the full pipeline: unsupported statements per reel, tokens and cost.
201	
202	Scorecards are committed as JSON and Markdown, failures included.
203	
204	## 10. Testing
205	
206	Unit tests for the parsers (checkpoint reader, test-runner output, trailer mapping), verifiers, grounding gate, redaction, budget and the runner's resume logic, written test-first. Fixture checkpoints are small synthetic trees built in the tests. One end-to-end test runs the pipeline with a mock model and a stub renderer.
207	
208	## 11. Privacy and safety
209	
210	Only public repositories. Redaction runs at ingest and again at the gate, and the gate fails closed. Reels about a repository are unlisted until its owner approves. Evaluation statistics about other people's repositories are published only in aggregate.

Roles map to models: editor and writer on a Claude Sonnet model, extractor on a small Claude model, entailment and `implemented` judge on a Nova model, vision on a Claude Sonnet model. Provider order: the hackathon gateway, then Venice on rate-limit, budget or server errors. A rate limiter stays under the gateway's 60 requests per minute. ### Hosting

## 7. Surfaces

| Route | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `/` | Landing: one claim, one call to action, a real reel playing |
| `/new` | Paste a repository URL, choose a window |
| `/r/[run]` | Live run: stages, events, cost so far |
| `/reel/[id]` | Player, evidence panel (each line and its sources), flags, cost, trace reference |
| `/inbox` | Reels waiting for approval or feedback |
| `/gallery` | Published reels |
| `/economics` | Plan versus actual cost per reel |
| `/health` | Evaluation scorecard, detections, open fixes for the agent itself |

Viewing is public. Starting a run is rate-limited per address and capped per day because every run costs money. Approving requires the owner token.

CLI: `dailies run <repo|path> [--since 24h] [--no-render] [--out dir]`, `dailies verify <repo|path>`.

## 8. Failure handling

| Failure | Response |
|---|---|
| Repo has no checkpoints | Run ends early with a clear message; nothing is rendered |

| Budget reached mid-run | Run stops in `blocked`, partial artifacts kept |
| Text-to-speech fails | Retry, alternate voice, then captions-only cut labelled as such |
| Render crashes | Retry the stage from its inputs; storyboard and audio are reused |
| Review still failing after two loops | Run ends in `blocked` with the findings attached |

| Entire CLI enrichment unavailable | Marked `skipped`; the run continues on git data |

## 9. Evaluation

- **Mutation benchmark.** For every verified `tests_pass` or `build_passes` claim, flip the recorded tool result to a failure; the verdict must become contradicted. For every contradicted one, flip it to a pass; the verdict must become verified. This shows a green verdict is never vacuous.

Scorecards are committed as JSON and Markdown, failures included.

Unit tests for the parsers (checkpoint reader, test-runner output, trailer mapping), verifiers, grounding gate, redaction, budget and the runner's resume logic, written test-first. Fixture checkpoints are small synthetic trees built in the tests. One end-to-end test runs the pipeline with a mock model and a stub renderer.

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.
